intro: Eleven hundred metres down, the cable went slack and the radio went strange. What came back up the line was not speech.
echo: Soldiers once lived for years in long ditches; the sea keeps one seven miles deep.

puzzles.title: Siphon
puzzles.flavor: Up and down, up and down: three rows, one long sentence, and not a single space left.

blocks.text: TAHTP TYBRE ETDDR HLSTI GHOEA OTPDE OEHLN WNDAW SIEET NERRE FTIEE AV

hints: Rail-fence transposition of a sentence with the spaces removed. Try 2 to 5 rails; the sentence tells you the answer.
To check you're on track: the answer begins with D.

puzzles.title: Thermocline
puzzles.flavor: The spy's handbook said to always carry a novel. It never said which one; this page will have to do.

blocks.text: Eleven hundred metres down, the cable went slack and the radio went strange. What came back up the line was not speech.

hints: Each pair is word.letter into the recovered page (words split on spaces; punctuation ignored).
To check you're on track: the answer begins with B.

puzzles.title: Marine Snow
puzzles.flavor: Three letters to a strip. The strips are in order; the sentence isn't.
hints: The sentence was cut into three-letter fragments (spaces removed) and alphabetised. Reassemble it using the word lengths; it tells you the answer.
To check you're on track: the answer begins with C.

puzzles.title: Sounding Line
puzzles.flavor: Cross off everything you recognise. What nobody claims is what you came for.

blocks.text: Hidden in the grid: 9 words to do with the bathysphere (lengths 4, 4, 5, 5, 5, 5, 5, 6, 7), running in any direction.

hints: Find every hidden word (any of 8 directions). The unused letters, read left-to-right, top-to-bottom, spell the answer.
The hidden words are: ANCHOR, CORAL, CRAB, CURRENT, KELP, SHARK, SONAR, SQUID, WHALE.
To check you're on track: the answer begins with U.

puzzles.title: Snow That Falls Upward
puzzles.flavor: Seat them correctly first. Then each guest owes you the letter of their name that matches their seat number.

clues: Anita sits somewhere to the left of Humphrey.
Bertrand and Humphrey are not neighbours.
Antonia sits somewhere between Bertrand and Dominic.
Xanthe sits somewhere to the left of Antonia.
Exactly 3 people sit between Dominic and Xanthe.
Exactly 4 people sit between Dominic and Hector.
Humphrey sits somewhere between Anita and Antonia.

hints: A logic puzzle: use the clues to find the one seating that works (seats are numbered 1 to n from the left). Then the guest in seat k gives the k-th letter of their name.
To check you're on track: the answer begins with B.

puzzles.title: Pressure Hull
puzzles.flavor: The note aboard the bathysphere was written round and round the page, from the edge towards the middle.
hints: A sentence was written into the grid along a spiral, starting in one corner and winding inward. Find the corner and the direction, read the sentence (dots are padding), and it tells you the answer.
To check you're on track: the answer begins with J.

meta.title: Meta: The Bathysphere Logs
meta.flavor: Everything aboard the bathysphere has a place, and every place is exactly the right size.
hints: Each answer fits exactly one row of the grid by length; the shaded squares, top to bottom, spell the final answer.
To check you're on track: the final answer begins with T.
